title: slaptain — mesh state
description: ADR-033, this site: one mesh's SlapdCluster and SlapdDatabase state from CR status via kube-state-metrics (Surface 1), the operator's own cross-pod and cross-site observations (Surface 2), and slapd's own cn=Monitor via the exporter sidecar (Surface 3). Monitoring is site-local: this dashboard shows whatever site its data source scrapes. Scoped data source → namespace → mesh → cluster.

options.content:
**Surface 1 of ADR-033** — slaptain's own recorded state, exported by kube-state-metrics' `custom-resource-state` from what the operator already wrote to CR status. No slaptain code, no operator release, no agent on the data plane.

**Monitoring is site-local** (ADR-033 amendment 2026-10-09): this site's Prometheus scrapes only this site, so everything here is this site — there is no `site` label and no site selector. Other sites appear only where this site's operator reports on them, as `peer`. To look at another site, pick its data source above.

**Scope follows the data model, which is namespace-local at every hop:** a namespace holds one or more meshes; a mesh is referenced by 0..n SlapdClusters; a cluster by 0..n SlapdDatabases and SlapdSchemas. So a mesh is identified by *(namespace, name)* — the name alone is not unique — and the selectors are chained in that order. `mesh` is single-select because a headline like *links synced* is a ratio over one mesh's links and an "All" would merge two meshes into one meaningless number. `cluster` is multi-select because a site may run several clusters of one mesh, and every row label names its cluster for that reason.

Database series carry no mesh of their own — only `cluster` — so they are scoped through the chosen mesh's cluster set rather than by label. A cluster with no `meshRef` carries no `mesh` label and does not appear here at all.

panels.title: Cross-site links synced
panels.description: Share of this site's outbound cross-site links in the selected mesh whose per-database CSN verdict is Synced, over every selected cluster. It is this site's consumer view only; the reverse direction is on each peer's own dashboard. Topology-independent: a peer or cluster added or removed moves the denominator, not the threshold.

panels.title: Clusters
panels.description: SlapdClusters of this mesh at this site answering this scrape. A cluster that stops answering drops out; it does not read healthy.

panels.title: Read-write pods ready
panels.description: Ready over desired, summed across the selected clusters.

panels.title: Oldest peer check
panels.description: Age of the least recent CSN check. The operator's pass runs on a 60s tick; if this climbs it has stopped observing, and every other panel is holding a last-known value rather than reporting health. If the series disappears entirely the operator skipped the check — see SlaptainPeerUnverified.

panels.title: Cross-site links — outbound from this site
panels.description:
One row per cluster per peer, from this site's consuming side. The verdict word rides in the row label: Synced, Lagging, PartiallyVerified or Unreachable. PartiallyVerified means at least one database yielded no readable contextCSN — unproven, not healthy (ADR-008). Peer status is consumer-side and one-directional, so the peer's view of this site is a row on the PEER's dashboard, and the two may legitimately disagree.

A row reading 'no connection' with an EMPTY verdict is a peer the operator never checked — since the 2026-10-06 fix only a cluster with no databases does that (SlaptainPeerUnverified).

defaults.noValue: nothing recorded for this scope — a mesh may legitimately have no clusters, and a cluster no databases

panels.title: Cluster conditions
panels.description: The reason is part of the row label because the reasons carry different meaning and different alert fuses. The two ReplicationMode*WiringRequired conditions are deliberately NOT shown: their semantics are inverted (True means a human still owes the cluster some wiring), so a healthy peer-mode cluster reports one True and one False and a red/green reading of them would be wrong.

defaults.noValue: nothing recorded for this scope — a mesh may legitimately have no clusters, and a cluster no databases

panels.title: Database conditions
panels.description:
Scoped through the mesh's cluster set, since a SlapdDatabase knows only its clusterRef and both refs resolve within one namespace.

DataPresent with reason GlueSuffix is the ADR-025 failure: one pod's suffix entry demoted to a hidden glue entry, every CSN signal reading clean, backups from that pod unrestorable. It never heals itself, so its alert carries no `for` at all.

defaults.noValue: nothing recorded for this scope — a mesh may legitimately have no clusters, and a cluster no databases

panels.title: Cross-site CSN lag
panels.description: Absent on a healthy link, by design — the operator only sets lagSeconds while the verdict is Lagging, and this panel shows the absence rather than a zero (ADR-033 decision 5). Also absent on an idle-but-broken link: lag is only observable while writes flow, which is why link state above is the primary signal and this is the magnitude behind it.

defaults.noValue: no lag reported — every selected link's verdict is Synced, or no writes are flowing

panels.title: Peer check age
panels.description: Per-link version of the headline stat. A sawtooth between 0 and ~60s is the operator's CSN tick working. A monotonic climb past the line is an operator that stopped observing; a row vanishing is one that never ran the check at all.

options.content:
**Surface 2 of ADR-033** — what the operator observed on its own pass and never wrote to CR status: the per-database CSN evidence counts behind the `ReplicationConverged` boolean above, the measured spread, the providers each cross-site link resolved to, and the ADR-025 suffix probe **per pod**. Scraped from this site's own operator through its ServiceMonitor.

**Absence is a reading here, and it is never zero.** A panel below that is blank, or a line with a gap in it, means the operator could not take that measurement — not that the measurement came back clean. Each panel says what its own absence means. Nothing on this surface is fresher than the operator's 60s tick, and the two *observation age* stats are what tell you whether the rest of it is a current reading or a frozen one.

panels.title: Oldest cluster observation
panels.description: Age of the least recent completed cluster pass, over the selected scope. The cluster controller requeues on a 60s tick while replication is enabled, so this should sawtooth under a minute. A monotonic climb means the pass is returning early — spec.suspend, an unresolvable meshRef, or a restore in progress — and every other Surface 2 panel is then showing a frozen reading that still looks healthy. A cluster with replication DISABLED has no periodic requeue at all (ADR-002 amendment) and will climb here for ever while being perfectly fine; that is why the alert rule is gated and this stat is not.

defaults.noValue: no cluster observation recorded — the operator is not exporting Surface 2, or has never completed a pass

panels.title: Oldest database observation
panels.description: Same question for the SlapdDatabase pass, which carries the per-pod suffix probes. Its guaranteed floor is the 5-minute resync interval, so up to ~300s here is normal even on a healthy database; on a cluster with external peers it tracks the 60s cluster tick instead, because the controller watches SlapdCluster and its lastChecked churn re-triggers it.

defaults.noValue: no database observation recorded — no SlapdDatabase has completed a pass in this scope

panels.title: CSN evidence gathered
panels.description: (pod, database) pairs that yielded a readable contextCSN, over the pairs the pass set out to read. Anything under 1 means the convergence verdict above is being judged on partial evidence, and unreadable evidence never counts toward healthy (ADR-008). A present 0 is the 2026-10-06 incident shape: attempted every pair, read not one.

defaults.noValue: no CSN measurement attempted — replication is off, or fewer than two pods are ready

panels.title: Pods carrying a GLUE suffix
panels.description: ADR-025: a multi-site seed race demoted a pod's suffix entry to a permanent hidden glue entry. It never heals, it reads clean on every CSN signal, and every backup taken from that pod is unrestorable. The series is emitted only for an affected pod, so a healthy mesh shows the no-value text rather than a zero — which is the point: there is nothing here to mistake for a measurement.

defaults.noValue: none — no pod reports a glue suffix entry

panels.title: contextCSN spread across pods
panels.description:
Newest minus oldest contextCSN timestamp across the read-write pods that answered, per database. This is the MAGNITUDE behind ReplicationConverged, which is an exact set comparison and so reads the same for half a second of propagation and for a pod frozen since yesterday.

**A gap in a line is not a zero.** The series is ABSENT below two readable pods, because a 0 there would read as perfect convergence for a measurement nobody took (ADR-033 decision 5). A measured 0 — two or more pods that agree — is drawn as a point on the zero line; an absent one leaves a hole, because spanNulls is off. If a line stops, read the CSN evidence stat, not this panel.

defaults.noValue: no spread measured anywhere in scope — fewer than two pods answered for every database, which is an absence of evidence and not a clean reading

panels.title: CSN evidence per database — pairs read of expected
panels.description:
The two absolute counts behind the ratio, per database. They are two counts rather than one ratio because a ratio has to divide by a count that can be 0. `read` dropping below `expected` while `expected` holds steady is pods going unreadable; both dropping together is a database leaving the pass.

A present 0 on `read` means every pair was attempted and every one failed — the attempt is the observation. An absent series means the pass never looked at that database at all.

defaults.noValue: no CSN pass recorded in scope

panels.title: Suffix entry per pod (ADR-025)
panels.description:
The per-pod suffix probe, which exists nowhere in CR status — the DataPresent condition above is the aggregate verdict over pods, and this is which pod.

A row that STOPS is a pod that could not be probed, and that is not the same as a pod that probed badly: suffixprobe reports positive evidence only, so no sample is emitted for a pod the pass could not reach. `role` is on the row because an RO consumer mid-initial-sync and an RW pod with a corruption both read 'missing' and only one of them is transient (ADR-025, 2026-09-14 amendment).

defaults.noValue: no pod was probed in this scope — absence of a probe is not a clean probe

panels.title: Discovered providers per cross-site link
panels.description:
How many remote pods each external peer's discovery resolved to. A link that resolved to nothing is how a cross-site outage begins (ADR-031, ADR-032), so a present 0 is alertable on its own.

The 0 and the gap mean different things and point at different sites. A present 0 says discovery RAN against the remote API and it reported no running slapd pods — look at the PEER. A gap says discovery could not be asked at all (a rotated or unparseable kubeconfig Secret, an unreachable remote API) — look at THIS site, and at the 'Cross-site links' panel above, which carries that case as Unreachable.

defaults.noValue: no discovery result in scope — either no cluster here declares an external peer, or discovery could not be asked at any of them

panels.title: Surface 3 — slapd itself, per pod (exporter sidecar) · full detail: “slaptain — slapd” dashboard

options.content:
**Surface 3 of ADR-033** — slapd's own `cn=Monitor`, read by the exporter sidecar on every slapd pod and scraped through the operator chart's `slapdPodMonitor`. Empty unless the SlapdCluster has `spec.monitoring.enabled` **and** this site's operator chart has `slapdPodMonitor.enabled`. Series carry `namespace`, `pod`, `cluster` and `role` from the scrape target and `suffix`, `op` or `direction` from the exporter's curated families (ADR-033 decision 4); there is no `mesh`, so they are scoped through the mesh's cluster set. **A missing line is not a zero**: a database opened before `cn=Monitor` has no LMDB statistics until its pod restarts, and a failed read drops the whole scrape's `cn=Monitor` families.

**Per-pod detail** — threads, waiters, traffic, every operation type, uptime and restarts, and a table of every database — is on the **slaptain — slapd** dashboard (link at the top; clicking a line in the panels below opens it on that pod).

panels.title: LMDB map fill per pod × database
panels.description: (pages_used − pages_free) / pages_max per database (suffix) per pod — the share of the map actually in use, against olcDbMaxSize, which can only be raised by recreate (ADR-024). pages_used alone is a high-water mark: it never shrinks after deletes, and pages_free is what LMDB will reuse. The cn=accesslog-* journals are here too; they fill with write rate and purge age, not with directory size. A full map refuses every write to that database. Same expression as the alert rules. Thresholds follow the rules: 80%/90% for data databases, 70%/85% for the cn=accesslog-* journals — the lines drawn are the data-database ones; the slaptain — slapd dashboard draws the journals on their own panel with their own.

defaults.noValue: no LMDB statistics in scope — exporter off, not scraped, or every database opened before cn=Monitor

panels.title: Current connections per pod
panels.description: openldap_connections_current, from cn=Current,cn=Connections,cn=Monitor. Steady growth over hours with no matching client load is the missing-olcIdleTimeout symptom: connections that are never reaped until the descriptor limit is hit.

defaults.noValue: no connection count in scope — exporter off, not scraped, or cn=Monitor unreadable

panels.title: Queued operations per pod
panels.description: openldap_threads_pending, from cn=Pending,cn=Threads,cn=Monitor: operations accepted and waiting to be handed to a worker thread. It is NOT a saturation signal: live it read above zero with only 2–9 of 16 threads active, so a non-zero value does not mean every worker is busy, and no alert rule watches it. Read it as queue depth next to the operation rate below.

defaults.noValue: no queue readings in scope — exporter off, not scraped, or cn=Monitor unreadable

panels.title: Exporter target per pod
panels.description: Prometheus' own up for each exporter sidecar (job slapd-exporter). Down means the scrape failed — pod gone, port blocked, sidecar crashed. Up says only that the sidecar answered: if slapd itself could not be read, the scrape still succeeds and carries no cn=Monitor families, which the panels to the left show as missing lines.

defaults.noValue: no exporter target in scope — spec.monitoring.enabled or slapdPodMonitor.enabled is off

panels.title: Operations per second per pod
panels.description: Completed LDAP operations per second (rate of openldap_operations_completed_total, slapd's monitorOpCompleted, over every operation type), per pod. The view that shows a replication storm: a stale-cookie full-refresh loop reads as hundreds of binds and searches per second on the affected pods while their peers stay flat, and nothing in Surfaces 1 or 2 moves. No alert rule — there is no load level that is wrong in itself.

defaults.noValue: no operation counters in scope — exporter off, not scraped, or cn=Monitor unreadable
